newsitem.title: USA: Judge in Prudential case won't remove himself.
newsitem.headline: Judge in Prudential case won't remove himself.

text.p: U.S. District Judge Alfred Wolin on Friday denied a motion asking that he remove himself from a class-action settlement case involving Prudential Insurance Co of America.
The request was made earlier this month by Pittsburgh attorney Michael Malakoff, who questioned Wolin's impartiality in the case.
Earlier this year, Prudential agreed to pay at least $410 million to settle lawsuits by policyholders claiming they were victims of deceptive sales practices.
He said he would consider the fairness of the proposed settlement at a hearing scheduled for January 21 in Newark.
In his remarks to the court, Wolin denied there had been any bias or partiality on his part toward any of the participants in the case.
In addition, he denied he had held any private meetings with Prudential Chairman Arthur Ryan, as Malakoff claimed.
Wolin said he met with Ryan twice but that others were present at those meetings, and there was nothing improper about them.
"To assert, as Mr Malakoff has asserted, that the rulings of this court has favored Prudential belie the record," Wolin told the court.
Wolin emphasized that the court has conducted the proceeds fairly and without bias.
Melvyn Weiss, one of the lead attorneys negotiating the settlement for the policyholders, said he opposed the request that Wolin disqualify himself from the case.

The proposed settlement could cost Prudential as much as $1.2 billion and could have a total value of almost $2.0 billion based on an expert opinion provided by accounting firm Arthur Andersen, Weiss said.
